*Saraṇaduka, Pītittika* is a canonical Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text belongs to the dual and triple matrix classifications of the *Paṭṭhāna*, systematically examining conditional relations through the intersection of the *saraṇa-duka* (the dyad of states accompanied by defilement or free from defilement) and the *pīti-ttika* (the triad of states associated with rapture) [SuttaCentral].

No independent English translation is listed on SuttaCentral, and no parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are recorded [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated analysis by DharmaNexus reflects extensive Pali-internal text reuse typical of the combinatorial permutations in the *Paṭṭhāna*, identifying 245 matching passages across 54 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its highest levels of formulaic overlap occur with other sections within the collection, particularly *Saraṇaduka, Hetudukādi* (Patthana 18.25; 19 matches, spanning segments §1.1–4.1 against §6.1_0–7.1), *Saraṇaduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.14; 22 matches), *Tika Kusalattika* (Patthana 5.2; 13 matches), and *Piṭṭhiduka, Sanidassanattika* (Patthana 21.55; 11 matches) [DharmaNexus]. High-similarity passages are also shared with adjacent sections in the same chapter, including *Saraṇaduka, Vitakkattika* (Patthana 15.75) and *Saraṇaduka, Vedanāttika* (Patthana 15.71) [DharmaNexus]. The surveyed secondary literature contains no direct citations or extended discussions of this specific section.
